# After increasing process priority, ros2_control still exhibits large jitter; what is the specific source confirmed by the real-time thread?

> **Current answer:** The author observed jitter in the real-time control loop after configuring real-time group limits and attempting to adjust process and child process priorities. A/B testing confirmed the jitter was caused by I2C IMU read, and the issue was resolved by isolating the I/O from the real-time path. The problem was not fixed by using a low-latency kernel alone. The effective fix was to isolate the I/O and observe stable behavior after removal or isolation. The credibility is limited as there is no formal cross-verification or independent replication available.

## Problem and symptoms

- How should I2C read and the update period parameter be diagnosed when the ros2_control 250 Hz control loop exhibits large jitter?
- Actual time difference fluctuates between ~1.1-6.9 ms; the update() period parameter does not match the author's offline time difference.

## Environment

- Raspberry Pi 5; controller_manager 250 Hz; low-latency kernel; real-time group limits configured afterward; not precise version of ROS 2/ros2_control used.

## Priority diagnostics

- Remove or isolate I2C IMU read and observe control loop jitter resolution.
- Do not use the same phenomenon to qualitatively determine the period parameter; print current_time, previous_time, and measured_period in the ros2_control node at the same location.

## Possible causes

- The author confirmed the large jitter comes from the I2C IMU read; the period parameter issue remains undiagnosed.

## Attempts

- Configure real-time group limits; use chrt to adjust process and child process priorities; disable I2C IMU read; maintainers suggest printing time variables.

## Effective fixes

- Remove/isolate the I2C IMU read to resolve the jitter observed by the author.

## Result

- I2C-related jitter confirmed by the author via A/B testing; update period parameter issue not closed-loop.

- Avoid unbounded blocking I/O in real-time control threads; monitor worst-case execution time and deadline miss.
